best_for: a single trend over evenly-spaced time
notes: direct-label the end point instead of a legend

best_for: a single trend where magnitude/volume reads better filled
notes: avoid stacking a lone series; a fill implies cumulative to some readers

best_for: compare a few trends over the same time axis
notes: past ~6 lines it becomes spaghetti; switch to small-multiples

best_for: many trends where each needs its own frame
notes: share one y-axis scale across facets so comparison stays honest

best_for: compare one value across a handful of nominal categories
notes: start the value axis at zero; sort by value unless the order is natural

best_for: compare one value across many categories with long labels
notes: horizontal keeps labels readable; sort descending

best_for: rank many categories where solid bars get visually heavy
notes: lighter ink than bars at high category counts

best_for: compare 2-4 series within each category
notes: keep groups small; more than 4 series per group is unreadable

best_for: one share-of-total with very few slices
notes: cap at ~5 slices; label values, never rely on angle alone

best_for: compare composition across categories that each sum to 100
notes: good for shares; annotate segment values

best_for: nested share where the slice count defeats a pie
notes: needs value labels; area is hard to compare precisely

best_for: a multi-level part-to-whole hierarchy
notes: rings past 3 levels lose legibility; offer a table

best_for: a strict parent-child hierarchy with magnitude
notes: rectangular is easier to label than a radial layout

best_for: the relationship between two numeric variables
notes: add a trend line; alpha-blend to reveal density

best_for: a correlation when points overplot heavily
notes: bins beat overplotted dots past ~2k points

best_for: two axes plus an encoded size dimension
notes: area-encode (not radius) the third variable; cap the bubble count

best_for: the shape of one continuous variable
notes: bin width is the story; state it in the caption

best_for: the median, spread and outliers of a distribution
notes: annotate the five-number summary for screen readers

best_for: compare distributions across groups
notes: order groups by median for a readable progression

best_for: compare full distribution shapes across a few groups
notes: only when shape (bimodality) matters; otherwise a box plot

best_for: quantified flow between stages or nodes
notes: cap the node count; label link magnitudes

best_for: mutual flows among a closed set of entities
notes: hard to read past ~15 nodes; offer the matrix

best_for: sequential drop-off through strictly ordered stages
notes: stages must be sequential; show absolute and percent

best_for: one metric across two categorical axes
notes: use a colorblind-safe sequential scale; label sparse cells

best_for: a rate or ratio mapped to bounded regions
notes: map rates not raw counts; pair with a ranked table

best_for: discrete located events or sites
notes: cluster dense points; size by magnitude, not color alone

best_for: one KPI against a target and qualitative bands
notes: more honest and compact than a gauge

best_for: a single headline metric with an optional delta
notes: pair the number with a sparkline for context

best_for: a headline metric plus its recent trend
notes: the sparkline gives shape; the number gives precision

best_for: a running total accumulating over time
notes: make cumulative-vs-incremental explicit in the title

best_for: how parts of a whole shift over time
notes: unstable middle bands mislead; cap series and order by size

best_for: a min-max or confidence band around a time series
notes: encode the band with fill plus a labeled bound, not color alone

best_for: values above and below a meaningful zero
notes: center on zero; use a colorblind-safe diverging pair with signs

best_for: a rank or value change between two points in time
notes: direct-label both ends; ideal for exactly two periods

best_for: rank movement across several periods
notes: lines encode rank not value; annotate ties

best_for: compare a few entities across shared axes
notes: only for <=4 series and a stable axis order; else a table

best_for: compare many records across several numeric axes
notes: allow axis reordering; brush to filter

best_for: entities and the relationships between them
notes: force layout is non-deterministic; provide an edge list

best_for: term or category frequency
notes: prefer a ranked bar over a word cloud (area is unreadable)

best_for: agreement or sentiment across ordered response categories
notes: center on the neutral midpoint; order by net-positive
